meta.description: Caregiver / family-member external dose after discharge of a radionuclide-therapy patient: proximity profiles, evaluation criteria per category, references and model assumptions.
meta.origin: Port of the author's workbook Dosis_acompanantes_simple_v2.1.xlsx (sheets Dosis, Curva and Comprobación).

kinetic_presets_note: A preset fills the radiopharmaceutical, the end of the fast phase, the effective half-lives, the number of cycles and the proximity profile. It never changes the measured discharge rate, the discharge time, the category or the cohabitation table. Literature values describe a cohort, not the patient.

kinetic_presets.label: Lu-177-PSMA-617 — Demir (2016) / Kurth (2018)
kinetic_presets.source: Source-workbook default. T fast 16.4 h is consistent with the mean dose rates at 1 m of Demir et al. (2016) Table 1, 15 µSv/h at 6 h and 7 µSv/h at 24 h: 18 h · ln 2 / ln(15/7) = 16.37 h. T slow 40.5 h: mean effective half-life after 48 h, Kurth et al. (2018) (cohort range 21.7–85.7 h). 6 cycles as in Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025).

kinetic_presets.label: Lu-177-PSMA-617 — Gayol Vilorio (2025)
kinetic_presets.source: Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025), Tables 4 and 6: Tef,1 = 22 h (median of the early mono-exponential fits, 12–24 h post-infusion, Table 2), Tef,2 = 42 h (median of the late values), 6 cycles; fast phase until 24 h post-infusion.

kinetic_presets.label: Lu-177-DOTATATE — Gayol Vilorio (2025)
kinetic_presets.source: Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025), Tables 3 and 5: Tef,1 = 25 h (median of the early mono-exponential fits, Table 2), Tef,2 = 55 h (median of the late values), 4 cycles; fast phase until 24 h post-infusion.

kinetic_presets.label: Lu-177-DOTATATE — Monserrat Fuertes (2023)
kinetic_presets.source: Monserrat Fuertes et al. (2023), Table 2, 20 patients: median Teff from the 6 h and 24 h values 25 h (range 12–92 h); median Teff from the 24, 48 and 168 h values 58 h (range 35–119 h); 4 cycles of 7.4 GBq. In that cohort patients were discharged at 24 h with a median rate at 1 m of 5.4 µSv/h.

kinetic_presets.label: I-131 (NaI) — thyroid remnant ablation, Foro (2011)
kinetic_presets.source: Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.B, Table 3.B 3: «Tef (vida media efectiva) = 3 días», single exponential. In the Forum's equations Tef = 1/λ (mean life), so the effective half-life is 3 d · ln 2 = 49.9 h; with this reading the app reproduces Tables 3.B 3 and 3.B 4 (partner < 60 years, 2 mSv), with the half-life reading it does not. In-patients for 48–72 h.

kinetic_presets.label: I-131 (NaI) — thyroid cancer metastases, Foro (2011)
kinetic_presets.source: Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.B, Table 3.B 4: «T.ef. (vida media efectiva) = 5 días» = 1/λ, i.e. effective half-life 5 d · ln 2 = 83.2 h. Single exponential.

kinetic_presets.label: I-131 (NaI) — hyperthyroidism, Foro (2011)
kinetic_presets.source: Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.C, Table 3.C 2: «T.ef. (vida media efectiva) = 7,2 días», computed with the equation of Annex 3.B, where Tef = 1/λ: effective half-life 7.2 d · ln 2 = 119.8 h. Single exponential from discharge; the thyroid uptake peaks at 24–48 h, so early urinary excretion of an out-patient is not modelled. Usually out-patient; the Forum gives this table by administered activity (185–800 MBq), the app needs the rate measured at 1 m.

own.distances_note: Complete the own-measurement table (1 m row fixed by the discharge rate).

categories.label: Carer ≤ 60 years
categories.basis: EC RP 97 (1998), table 1, and Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), table 2: 3 mSv for adults up to 60 years — more restrictive than the international 5 mSv per episode (ICRP 103 [7], para. 351). RD 601/2019, arts. 6.2, 7 and 8, requires carer constraints but sets no value

categories.label: Carer > 60 years
categories.basis: ICRP 103 (2007), para. 351, and ICRP 94 (2004): 5 mSv per episode for carers; IAEA SSG-46 (2018), para. 2.49: usually 5 mSv per episode for adult carers, less severe constraints allowed for elderly people. Adopted by Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025) instead of the 15 mSv of EC RP 97 and the Forum

categories.label: Public (adult, child or pregnant woman)
categories.basis: RD 1029/2022, art. 15: public annual limit, applied to the whole treatment; ICRP 94 (2004) and ICRP 103, para. 351: the public limit applies to infants, children and casual visitors

categories.label: Co-worker
categories.basis: EC RP 97 (1998) and Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), table 2 (p. 13): 0.3 mSv for third persons

criteria_note: Evaluation criteria adopted by the department, not values fixed by regulation for this treatment. Scope: one person, the whole treatment (all cycles together) — the ICRP «episode» (the duration of a given release after therapy) is applied to the complete treatment, which is the more restrictive reading. Carers are people who, outside their occupation, knowingly and voluntarily help in the care of the patient (RD 601/2019, art. 7.1); children and pregnant women are assessed with the public category. The criterion only changes the comparison and the inverse calculations, never the calculated dose.
assumptions: Time model: two consecutive, continuous exponentials. At the end of the fast phase the rate reached is kept. It is not a simultaneous sum of components.
Occupancy h/24 is a daily average, not an exact timetable. Single trips and contacts concentrated during the fast phase require a specific time-resolved assessment.
Spatial factors are taken as constant in both phases. Body redistribution can change them: justify their use for the time of discharge and the case.
Equal cycles: same discharge rate, kinetics and cohabitation. Multiplying by the number of cycles assumes the pattern repeats with no relevant change from overlapping cycles.
Distances: keep the same origin, posture and orientation as the profile or measurement protocol. Do not confuse the separation between surfaces with the distance to a geometric centre.
Approximate profiles: published conventions, not universal measured factors. No automatic interpolation or extrapolation: the distance is chosen from the profile list.
Own measurements: enter distances and the rates at those distances, measured at the same time as the 1 m reading. Record the protocol. Do not repeat distances.

Discharge time and end of the fast phase are counted from administration. With the Kurth and Demir model the fast phase ends at 24 h. If discharge is later (or the end is 0) only the slow half-life is used, and the discharge rate must already belong to the slow phase.
Each cycle is integrated to infinity: with several weeks between cycles, practically the whole dose of a cycle is received before the next one.
inverse_note: Maximum rate: the discharge rate that exactly exhausts the criterion with the restrictions of the table (the dose is proportional to the rate). Minimum restriction: days that exhaust the criterion applying the same duration to both rows; "Unattainable" = not met however long it lasts: contact during the restriction must be reduced. To apply it, enter the adopted restriction in the days column of the cohabitation table.
own_protocol_note: Own-measurement protocol to record: radiopharmaceutical, distance reference, posture, orientation and time of measurement.
references: [1] Monserrat Fuertes et al. (2023). Individualisation of radiation protection recommendations for patients treated with [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE. EJNMMI Physics 10:50. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40658-023-00570-7 — proximity factors (medians of measurements at 0.1, 0.5 and 1 m) and DOTATATE kinetics.

[2] Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011). Criterios de alta de pacientes y medidas para la protección radiológica del público después de tratamientos metabólicos con I-131 — contact taken at 0.4 m, I-131 kinetics, 3 mSv and 0.3 mSv criteria.

[3] Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025). Periodo de restricciones tras el alta en terapia con 177Lu-DOTATATE y 177Lu-PSMA-617. Rev. Fís. Méd. 26(2):27–36 — Lu-177 kinetics, contact at 0.4 m, 5 mSv over 60 years.

[4] Demir et al. (2016). Evaluation of radiation safety in 177Lu-PSMA therapy and outpatient treatment protocol. J. Radiol. Prot. 36(2):269. https://doi.org/10.1088/0952-4746/36/2/269 — dose rates at 1 m (PSMA fast phase).
[5] Kurth et al. (2018). External radiation exposure, excretion and effective half-life in 177Lu-PSMA-targeted therapies. EJNMMI Research 8:32 — slow effective half-life; fast phase ending at 24 h.
[6] ICRP Publication 94 (2004). Release of patients after therapy with unsealed radionuclides — 5 mSv per episode for relatives and caregivers; public limit for infants, children and casual visitors.
[7] ICRP Publication 103 (2007), para. 351 — 5 mSv per episode (the duration of a given release after therapy) for carers other than young children, used flexibly.
[8] IAEA SSG-46 (2018), para. 2.49 — usually 5 mSv per episode for adult carers; less severe constraints allowed for elderly people.
[9] European Commission, Radiation Protection 97 (1998), table 1 — I-131: children 1 mSv, adults up to 60 years 3 mSv, over 60 years 15 mSv; third persons 0.3 mSv.
[10] IAEA Safety Reports Series No. 63 (2009). Release of patients after radionuclide therapy — 5 mSv during the treatment (1996 BSS); Appendix II, limits of the inverse square law at short distance.

reference_cases.note: Reference cases of workbook v6 (Comprobación sheet B): restriction 3 d from discharge, 6 cycles, fast phase ending at 24 h. Carer: 6 h/d at 1 m during the restriction; afterwards 6 h/d at 1 m and 8 h/d in contact (factor 6.25) → fr = 0.25, fn = 2.3333. Non-carer adult: 6 h/d at 1 m with no shared rest → fr = fn = 0.25. Expected values rounded to 2 decimals.

profiles_note: The intermediate distances of the approximate profiles [2], [3] are model evaluations, not measurements, and 6.25 is not a measured ratio: the spatial ratios measured by Demir [4] vary with time. The d^-1.5 approximation of IAEA SRS-63 [10] is not adopted as a universal profile.
